title: Invariant rational functions and their normalized equivariant graph
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $N$ be a normal projective geometrically integral finite-type $k$-scheme, and let a finite group $H$ act semilinearly on $N$ and $k$. Put $E=k(N)$. Let $r\geq0$ and let $t_1,\ldots,t_r\in E$ be algebraically independent over $k$ and fixed by every element of $H$. Give $P=\mathbf P^r_k$ the action induced by that on $k$, fixing the homogeneous coordinates. There is an $H$-invariant dense open $V\subseteq N$ on which $[1:t_1:\cdots:t_r]$ defines an equivariant morphism $v:V\to P$. Let $Z$ be the scheme-theoretic closure of its graph in $N\times_kP$, and let $X'$ be the normalization of $Z$ in $E$. Then $Z$ is integral, the projection $Z\to N$ identifies $k(Z)$ with $E$ and is an isomorphism over $V$, and $X'$ is normal projective geometrically integral of finite type over $k$. The diagonal action on the graph extends to $Z$ and lifts to a semilinear action on $X'$. The resulting projections $a:X'\to N$ and $b:X'\to P$ are equivariant H-projective morphisms; $a$ is proper, surjective and birational and is an isomorphism over $V$, while $b$ is dominant and proper and induces precisely the inclusion $k(P)=k(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\subseteq E$.

The notions used are [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-sc-function-field], [def-sc-normalization], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis], [def-kun-transcendence-degree], [def-sfb-dominant-function-field-map]. Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. A projective morphism here means an H-projective morphism: it admits a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over its target. A semilinear $H$-action means actions by scheme automorphisms and by field automorphisms of $k$, with the structure morphisms equivariant; faithfulness is not assumed. A birational morphism here identifies the function fields and is an isomorphism over a dense open of the target.

proof.text: Write $\eta$ for the generic point of $N$. Represent each $t_i\in\mathcal O_{N,\eta}$ by a section on a neighbourhood of $\eta$, and intersect these finitely many neighbourhoods to obtain $U$. Set $V=\bigcap_{h\in H}h(U)$. Every translate contains $\eta$, so $V$ is a dense invariant open. On $V$ the sections define a ring map $k[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to\Gamma(V,\mathcal O_V)$, hence a morphism to the chart $D_+(T_0)\subset P$ by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme] and [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts]. Its composite is $v=[1:t_1:\cdots:t_r]$. For each $h$, the morphisms $v\circ h$ and $h_P\circ v$ land in this chart. Their pullbacks agree on coefficients by semilinearity and on $T_i/T_0$ because $t_i$ is fixed in $E$. These equalities of germs are equalities of sections by [lem-sc-integral-scheme-stalks-in-function-field], so the affine-morphism bijection gives equivariance. This uses representatives of germs, finite intersections and the cited coordinate descriptions.

source.place: Tag 01RV (lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions), generic-stalk representatives; Constructions Tag 01NG (lemma-standard-covering-projective-space), Schemes Tag 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine).

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0$ and $k$), hence $N$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], every open of $N$, including $V$, is quasi-compact. Put $M=N\times_kP$ and $j=(\mathrm{id},v):V\to M$. Projective space is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-proj-separated]. The graph $V\to V\times_kP$ is the pullback of its closed diagonal along $(v\circ\operatorname{pr}_V,\operatorname{pr}_P)$, hence a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Composing with the open immersion $V\times_kP\to M$ makes $j$ an immersion. It is quasi-compact: the preimage of any affine open of $M$ is an open of the Noetherian scheme $V$. Thus the scheme-image tools below have their quasi-compactness hypotheses.

source.place: Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), 01OW/01OZ (Noetherian opens); graph as base change of the separated diagonal; Constructions Tag 01MC (lemma-proj-separated).

proof.text: By [lem-trf-reduced-scheme-image], $Z=\operatorname{SIm}(j)$ is reduced with underlying space $\overline{j(|V|)}$. This space is nonempty and irreducible: $V$ is nonempty irreducible, and continuous images and closures preserve irreducibility. Hence $Z$ is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Apply [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-partial-section] to the quasi-compact open $V\hookrightarrow N$ and the separated $P\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. It makes $p:Z\to N$ an isomorphism over $V$. More precisely, $p^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an isomorphism and $j$ factors through its inverse, so $j(V)=p^{-1}(V)$ as an open subscheme of $Z$. This open is dense because its image is the original graph and $|Z|=\overline{j(|V|)}$. The generic point of $Z$ therefore lies in this open and maps to $\eta$; the generic stalk map of $p$ is the stalk map of that open isomorphism. This identifies $k(Z)$ with $E$ by actual pullback, using [def-sc-function-field].

Let $A_h$ be the diagonal automorphism of $M$. The equation $A_hj=jh$ shows that $A_h$ preserves the kernel ideal of $j$: a section vanishes after pullback along $j$ if and only if its transform vanishes, because pullback along $h$ is invertible. The affine kernel description in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-image-qc-kernel] therefore identifies the transformed defining ideal of $Z$ with itself. Restricting $A_h$ to this closed subscheme gives $h_Z$ with $c h_Z=A_h c$, where $c:Z\hookrightarrow M$. The restrictions obey the identity and multiplication laws: after composition with $c$ these are the laws for $A_h$, and a closed immersion is a monomorphism, as stated in the cited node. This gives a semilinear action, with both projections equivariant.

source.place: Tag 01R8 (lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image), affine kernel characterization and restriction of the diagonal action.

proof.text: Choose a closed immersion $e:N\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^m_k$ from projectivity. The map $e\times\mathrm{id}_P:M\to\mathbf P^m_k\times_k\mathbf P^r_k$ is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. Compose it with the Segre closed immersion of [lem-chow-segre] and with $c:Z\hookrightarrow M$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp] this embeds $Z$ in $\mathbf P^{(m+1)(r+1)-1}_k$. Thus $Z$ is projective in the finite-space convention [def-kun-projective], and proper by [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], hence of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The same projective-implies-proper result supplies properness of $N$ for the normalization tool.

source.place: Constructions Tag 01WD (lemma-segre-embedding); closed-immersion base change/composition; projective implies proper.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-equivariant-normal-projective-model] with its $X=N$, $T=Z$, $p:Z\to N$ and $U=V$. Steps 2--5 give integral finite-type projective $Z$, its semilinear action, equivariance of $p$, the specified field isomorphism and the isomorphism over $V$; $N$ is normal integral proper of finite type by hypothesis and step 5. The normalization $n:X'\to Z$ in $k(Z)=E$ is finite, surjective and birational. The cited statement gives $X'$ normal integral, projective and of finite type over $k$, the unique lifted semilinear action, and $a=pn$ equivariant, proper, surjective and H-projective, identifying $k(X')$ with $E$ and an isomorphism over $V$. Since $N$ is geometrically integral, its final clause gives geometric integrality of $Z$ and $X'$. Composing $n$ with the other projection defines the equivariant $b:X'\to P$.

source.place: Varieties Tag 0BXR (lemma-normalization-locally-algebraic); finite equivariant normalization tool; de Jong Lemma 5.2, printed p.613.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-projective-fibre-product-closed-model] with its $X=P$, separated over $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-proj-separated], $I=\{1\}$, $Y_1=X'$, $q_1=b$, a closed immersion $e_1:X'\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_k$ over $k$ from the projectivity of $X'$ in step 6 (its structure map is that of $P$ composed with the $k$-morphism $b$), and $c=\mathrm{id}$. The one-factor fibre product is $X'$ with $r=b$, so $b$ is H-projective, with a closed immersion into $\mathbf P^n_P$ over $P$, and proper. For dominance and the specified field map use $D_+(T_0)=\operatorname{Spec}k[T_1,\ldots,T_r]$. The standard charts have domain coordinate rings, and each overlaps $D_+(T_0)$ in the dense principal open obtained by inverting the nonzero coordinate $T_0/T_i$. Thus $P$ is integral and this chart is dense. At the generic point of $X'$, its coordinate map is $k[T_1,\ldots,T_r]\to E$, $T_i\mapsto t_i$, by the construction on $V$. Algebraic independence means exactly that its kernel is zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-field-point-residue-field] the generic point therefore maps to the zero prime, the generic point of $P$. Thus the image of $b$ contains a point whose closure is all of $P$, so $b$ is dominant. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], $k(P)=\operatorname{Frac}k[T_1,\ldots,T_r]$. The same residue-field statement identifies the induced map as the unique extension of polynomial evaluation, namely the inclusion $k(t_1,\ldots,t_r)\subset E$; [def-sfb-dominant-function-field-map] identifies it with the required generic stalk pullback. When $r=0$ these are the ring $k$ and $P=\operatorname{Spec}k$.
